clue.text: Paid for a bride's exotic, unusually shaped flower from Africa

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so the preceding letters come out in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A groom has paid for an exotic, oddly shaped African bloom for his bride's bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' looks like it describes the flower, but it works on the words before it; the whole of the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The strelitzia, a South African plant whose flowerhead resembles a bird's crested head and beak, is commonly called the bird of paradise.

clue.text: Lawyer seen in pub with a writ's later made to look silly

indicators.note: making something look silly means knocking it out of shape, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A lawyer is spotted in a pub, and a writ arriving late makes them look foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister-at-law is the full formal title of a barrister, a lawyer who pleads in the higher courts.

clue.text: More reliable? Not initially, being comparatively out of practice

indicators.note: not initially tells you to drop the opening letter of the word just found

blocks.note: trustier means more to be trusted

explanation.surface: Someone who is a bit rusty is said to be less dependable, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUSTIER without its T leaves RUSTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty describes skills weakened by lack of use, and rustier is its comparative form.

clue.text: Meet actor struggling to deliver line

indicators.note: struggling suggests flailing about out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A director meets an actor who is struggling to deliver a line on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' reads as a line of dialogue, but here it is a line of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An octameter is a line of poetry made up of eight metrical feet.

clue.text: Rising quietly and wandering aimlessly

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
roving means wandering without a fixed aim

explanation.surface: Someone getting up quietly and then drifting around with no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' sounds like getting out of bed, but it is the baker's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread dough proving is rising as the yeast works, before it is baked.

clue.text: Criminal in court causing uproar

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A criminal in the dock creates a disturbance in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the person in court, but it is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy disturbance or row, the same as an uproar.

clue.text: Fidel talks about US detention camp

indicators.note: the words are said to go about, or surround, what is wanted, so it sits inside them

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively across the two words

explanation.surface: Fidel Castro speaks about the American prison camp at Guantanamo Bay, on Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: fi(DEL TA)lks.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp Delta was the main detention facility at the US base at Guantanamo Bay in Cuba.

clue.text: Place is possibly unique

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of these letters

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a spot might be one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Special can mean distinctive or one of a kind, matching a looser sense of unique.

clue.text: Ms Jowell returns, exposing unsavoury business practice

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: Tessa Jowell was a British Labour cabinet minister
stripping means baring or uncovering

explanation.surface: A politician comes back and blows the whistle on a shady corporate habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Tessa Jowell was the minister who oversaw the London 2012 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Asset-stripping is buying a company cheaply and selling off its assets for profit, usually leaving it to collapse.

clue.text: Prepare to stir duck and rice dish

indicators.note: preparing food means working the ingredients up, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters of both words
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so a zero, O

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: get ready to stir duck into a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the meat going into the pot, but it is cricket's zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: They visit cellars, getting tipsy

definitions.note: a clause meaning people who visit, standing for a plural noun

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Visitors go down to the wine cellars and get a little drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Callers are people who drop in on someone, that is, visitors.

clue.text: Over in Bergamo, I discussed language

indicators.note: in says what is wanted lies inside the words that follow
over in a down-and-back sense means turned over, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively across these words

explanation.surface: An Italian in Bergamo talks about language with a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: berga(MO I DI)scussed read backwards gives IDIOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression, and by extension the characteristic speech or dialect of a people.

clue.text: I'm international mime artist, extremely versatile but unoriginal

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outermost letters of the word are used

blocks.note: taken as written
I is a standard abbreviation for international
Jacques Tati, the French comic actor and director known for mime
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A performer boasts of being a versatile world-class mime, yet is merely copying others.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati, creator of Monsieur Hulot, began as a mime artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitative work copies others rather than inventing, so it lacks originality.

clue.text: Get near to volatile harmful substance

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and liable to change, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A warning to approach an unstable, dangerous chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volatile' sounds like a property of the chemical, but it acts on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teratogen is an agent, such as a drug, that causes malformation of an embryo, so a dangerous substance.

clue.text: Jerks and dolts demanding change of leader

indicators.note: a change of leader means the first letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: dolts are fools

explanation.surface: Idiots and fools who insist on a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The D of DOLTS is replaced by J; 'Jerks' itself suggests the new initial, since it starts with J.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolt is a sudden jerk, so jolts and jerks are both sharp, abrupt movements.

clue.text: Minister is a knave to vacuously support improper war

indicators.note: vacuously means emptily, so the inside of the word is cleared out, leaving its ends
improper means not in proper order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the knave in a pack of cards is the jack
the first and last letters of the word
the letters of the word

explanation.surface: A politician is accused of being a scoundrel who blindly backs an unjust war.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was the UK Foreign Secretary at the time of the 2003 Iraq war, which gives the surface its sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Straw was a British Labour cabinet minister, serving as Home and Foreign Secretary.

clue.text: Hand over joint, but not Ecstasy

indicators.note: but not means excepting, so the named letter is left out

blocks.note: a reefer is a cannabis cigarette, a joint
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Pass the joint around, but no ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: REEFER with one E removed gives REFER.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else to deal with.

clue.text: Attached to insect? That's sweet!

blocks.note: fond of means attached to
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone who has grown fond of a bug is told how cute that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' reads as an exclamation of approval, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugar paste used as a confectionery and for icing cakes.

clue.text: Try to run; it will make you fitter

blocks.note: to exercise someone is to worry or try them
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Advice to go running, since it will get you in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try to run' looks like encouragement to go jogging; 'Try' is the verb meaning to tax or vex.
explanation.definitionFit: An exerciser is a machine or device used for physical workouts, which improves fitness.

clue.text: The Spanish girl finally got free lift

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
a girl's name
the last letters of both words

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl at last gets a ride at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to raise something up, the same as to lift it.

clue.text: Doctor, single, originally hailing from part of Britain

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order
originally points to the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the letters of the word
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An unmarried doctor who comes from one region of the UK.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person described, but it is an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: English describes a person or thing from England, one of the countries making up Britain.

clue.text: New Israeli composer

blocks.note: the letters of the word

explanation.surface: A newly arrived Israeli writer of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Salieri was an Italian classical composer, famous as Mozart's supposed rival.

clue.text: Former cricket captain with terribly trying ego

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A one-time skipper known for an exasperating sense of his own importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Greig was a South African-born all-rounder who captained the England Test side in the mid-1970s.

clue.text: Get hold of good tool

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a rasp is a coarse file, a tool

explanation.surface: Pick up a decent implement.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to seize it firmly, to take hold of it.

clue.text: Girl gets work in old county

blocks.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A young woman finds a job out in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: Salop is the former official name of Shropshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop was the name of the county of Shropshire from 1974 to 1980, so a county name now out of use.

clue.text: Allied leaders start to ascertain, by degrees, where Montgomery is

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letter of each word is taken
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letters of this word and the indicator word beside it
the opening letter of the word
BA and MA are university degrees

explanation.surface: The Allied commanders begin to find out, step by step, where General Montgomery has got to.
explanation.walkthrough: Initials of 'Allied leaders' give AL. 'Montgomery' looks like the British general, but it is the capital of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Montgomery is the state capital of Alabama, so the state is where that city lies.

clue.text: Ariel is, perhaps, from Tel Aviv?

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is a major city in Israel, so someone from there is an Israeli.

the first letters of both words
the first letter of the word
